cards.front: What are the key assumptions underlying the Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution?
cards.back: Classical ideal gas of N indistinguishable particles; velocities follow Boltzmann statistics (dilute, no quantum effects); collisions randomize directions but conserve energy; equilibrium at temperature T.

cards.front: Write the normalized probability density for a single velocity component $v_x$.
cards.back: $f(v_x)dv_x=\sqrt{\frac{m}{2\pi kT}}\exp(-mv_x^2/2kT)dv_x$. This follows from the Boltzmann factor $e^{-E/kT}$ with $E=\frac12mv_x^2$ and 1-D normalization.

cards.front: Derive the joint velocity distribution $f(v_x,v_y,v_z)$ from the three independent components.
cards.back: $f(\mathbf{v})=\left(\frac{m}{2\pi kT}\right)^{3/2}\exp(-m v^2/2kT)$, obtained by multiplying the three normalized 1-D Gaussians (isotropic, $v^2=v_x^2+v_y^2+v_z^2$).

cards.front: Explain the origin of the $4\pi v^2$ factor when converting from velocity to speed distribution.
cards.back: In velocity space the probability lies in a spherical shell of radius $v$ and thickness $dv$; the shell volume is $4\pi v^2 dv$. Hence $f(v)dv=f(\mathbf{v})\,4\pi v^2 dv$.

cards.front: Write the normalized Maxwell-Boltzmann speed distribution $f(v)$.
Derive the most probable speed $v_p$ by maximizing $f(v)$.
cards.back: Set $df/dv=0$: $v_p=\sqrt{2kT/m}$. This is the mode of the speed distribution.

cards.front: State the expressions for the mean speed $\langle v\rangle$ and rms speed $v_\text{rms}$.
cards.back: $\langle v\rangle=\sqrt{8kT/\pi m}$, $v_\text{rms}=\sqrt{3kT/m}$. Both obtained by evaluating the appropriate moments of $f(v)$.
